title: Long MU — HBM4 Cycle Re-Rating on SKHY Debut + TSMC +36% AI Demand Confirmation
entry: Long MU $955–995 at Monday July 13 open. MU is in a day-range of $954.13–$998.00 on July 13 as the market digests the SKHY debut (closed $168.01, +12.7% above $149 IPO price) alongside TSMC Q2 revenue +36% ($39.6B). Enter at market in the $955-995 zone; do not chase above $1,000 pre-CPI (July 14 release) as rate-hike concerns may generate an intraday reversal. Reserve 30% of allocation for a post-CPI add on July 14 if June CPI prints ≤3.5% (rate-relief read through benefits high-multiple tech including MU at ~30x forward earnings).
stop_loss: $880 daily close — approximately 10.1% below the $979 midpoint. A close at $880 would imply one of: (1) a hyperscaler pre-announcement of AI capex reduction (Google/Microsoft/AWS guiding lower on compute infrastructure); (2) MU-specific demand signal weakness — a channel check or sell-side survey suggesting HBM4 orders from NVDA are being rescheduled into H1 2027; (3) September rate hike probability rising above 85% triggering a broad high-multiple compression that disproportionately affects MU at 30x forward earnings; (4) BTC Gate 2 ($62,000) breach triggering a broader risk-off that pulls semi stocks below the July 9 lows ($925 MU level). Exit on a $880 close, no exceptions.
targets: $1,055 — SKHY ADR establishes two consecutive closes above $175 post-CPI (validating the HBM4 premium the US market is willing to pay) and MU re-rates proportionally as the US HBM4 compeitor; +7.8% from $979; cover 40% within 1-2 weeks

$1,130 — Microsoft Azure, Amazon AWS, or Google Cloud Q2 earnings (expected July 29-31) confirm AI compute capex acceleration above consensus; MU's HBM4 demand outlook for Q4 FY2026 (Sept quarter) and Q1 FY2027 locked in at record volumes; +15.4%; cover 40%

$1,200 — NVDA Q2 FY27 earnings August 26 confirm $91B guide and Blackwell Ultra HBM4 allocation rates above 60% of DRAM capacity; MU raises FY2027 HBM4 revenue guidance to $25B+; +22.6%; hold final 20%
risk_reward: 1:2.2 to third target (entry $979, stop $880 = risk $99; T3 $1,200 = reward $221)
catalyst: Two events over the weekend of July 12-13 converge to create a MU-specific re-rating opportunity. First, SKHY's Nasdaq ADR debut: SKHY closed at $168.01 — $19.01 above the $149 IPO price, a +12.7% first-day gain — on a day when the Seoul parent (SK Hynix KRX) fell 13% and the Kospi triggered a circuit-breaker. The US market is explicitly pricing a higher valuation multiple for HBM4 supply than the Korean market, and is specifically choosing to pay up for the HBM4 scarcity narrative even in the middle of a risk-off day. This is a direct read-through for MU as the US-listed HBM4 producer. Second, TSMC Q2 revenue +36% ($39.6B, June +68% YoY) confirms that AI training cluster demand is not slowing — it is accelerating. TSMC makes NVDA's chips; record TSMC revenue is a record NVDA chip order signal; record NVDA orders require record HBM4 (which MU supplies to NVDA directly, alongside SK Hynix).
thesis:
Micron Technology is the most direct US-listed beneficiary of the HBM4 cycle that the SKHY debut confirmed on July 13. SKHY's 7x oversubscription (announced July 9) and +12.7% first-day Nasdaq performance communicate a clear market judgment: the US investment community values HBM4 memory supply at a significant premium to conventional DRAM, and will pay through a risk-off day (Kospi circuit-breaker, Iran escalation, NQ -1.24%) to hold HBM4 exposure. MU provides this exposure as the sole US-based HBM4 manufacturer currently shipping to NVDA's Blackwell Ultra GPU platform.

MU's HBM4 market share is growing, not shrinking, relative to SK Hynix. SK Hynix held ~50% of HBM4 market share in Q1 2026; MU has guided to 30% HBM4 share by Q4 FY2026 (September 2026 quarter) as its 1-gamma DRAM node yields improve. This means MU's HBM4 revenue will be growing from a lower base than SK Hynix at the same time the total market is expanding. TSMC +36% revenue confirms the market is expanding. MU's June 2026 (Q3 FY2026) earnings beat of $50B in data-center revenue guidance underscores the strength of the near-term demand. SKHY's debut re-rates the entire HBM4 complex; MU is the US-listed version of that trade.

The rate-risk overlay is the complication. MU at $979 trades at approximately 30x forward earnings — a multiple that is sensitive to the September rate-hike probability curve. The July 14 CPI print (consensus 3.9% YoY) is the near-term gating event: a soft print (≤3.5%) would reduce September hike probability and directly support MU's multiple. A hot print (≥4.1%) would compress MU's multiple even as the HBM4 demand thesis strengthens. The stop at $880 captures this rate-compression scenario. The asymmetry works because the HBM4 thesis is structural (AI training demand is multi-year) while the rate-compression risk is cyclical (September hike vs. a hold are both temporary states).

The counter-party is the MU bear who argues: AI memory orders are front-loaded as hyperscalers secure supply in H1 2026 for H2 2026 training jobs. Once those jobs complete, HBM4 reorder rates slow in H1 2027, creating an inventory correction. MU at 30x forward earnings already prices in a perfect HBM4 cycle with no inventory correction. The SKHY debut premium may be front-running a demand level that MU cannot actually sustain. The bull response: TSMC's June foundry revenue (+68% YoY for the month alone) is not consistent with front-loaded demand — front-loading happens over quarters, not months. June 2026 running at +68% implies the H2 2026 AI training ramp is still in progress, not yet peaking.
bull_case: June 2026 CPI prints ≤3.5% on July 14, reducing September hike probability below 50%. SKHY ADR closes above $175 post-CPI for two consecutive sessions. MU re-rates to $1,060+ on HBM4 cycle validation + rate relief. Microsoft Azure Q2 earnings (July 29) confirm AI compute capex rising 45% YoY — above consensus 38%. MU raises FY2027 HBM4 revenue guidance to $23B (from $18B) at an August analyst day. Stock reaches $1,130 (T2) within 3 weeks of entry and holds toward $1,200 into NVDA's August 26 Q2 FY27 print.
bear_case: CPI prints 4.2% on July 14 — above consensus 3.9% and above the prior 4.0% reading — driven by Iran/Hormuz oil spike bleeding into June transport and energy sub-components. September rate hike probability spikes above 80%. MU falls from $979 toward $920-940 on rate-compression. SKHY ADR fails to hold $162 through July 15 (falls below July 10 close), signaling the HBM4 premium is not durable under rate pressure. Stop at $880 holds if the selloff is orderly; at $880 MU would be back at the post-Q3-earnings (June 24) settlement range, representing a reversal of the SKHY-debut premium.
invalidation: $880 daily close; OR any hyperscaler (Google, Microsoft, AWS, Meta) announces a reduction or delay in AI infrastructure capex spend for 2026 or 2027 (directly invalidates the HBM4 volume assumption); OR MU-specific guidance: MU issues a press release or 8-K indicating Q4 FY2026 HBM4 revenue will be below the $15B quarterly run-rate previously implied; OR SKHY ADR closes below the $149 IPO price on any day before July 21 (signals the US HBM4 re-rating premium was purely speculative and not fundamental); OR September rate hike probability reaches 85%+ and NQ declines more than 8% from July 9 highs (forces position-size reduction across high-multiple tech)

outcome.outcome_label: Stop at $880 triggered — SOX bear market + Kimi K3 disruption narrative
outcome.note: MU traded as low as $804 intraday on July 20 (range $804–$903) and settled around $849, well below the $880 daily-close stop trigger. The SOX entered an official bear market (–20%+ from June high) on the semiconductor position-clearing wave that began July 14–17. The Kimi K3 open-source AI model disruption thesis — claiming frontier AI performance at 70% compute cost reduction — has not been refuted and the full open-weight release July 27 adds a second structural overhang. MU's stop at $880 is the structural exit level. Exit recorded at $880 (stop trigger price); current market price $848.95.
